rationale: The golden submission is rejected because it genuinely mismatches the shipped RTL/testbench behavior, not because evaluate.py is buggy. Tracing the RTL in inputs/signature_compare.v: when running && !done, the module only evaluates a new byte pair on cycles where byte_valid is high AND checks 'else if (byte_count == 5'd15)' for a full-match terminal condition -- but byte_count is only ever incremented in the else-branch when there is NO mismatch, so byte_count correctly counts consumed matching bytes. The measured simulation shows mismatch at even positions (k=0,2,4,...) yields cycles_to_done=17 (not k+2 as golden claims), which is the full-match-length behavior, while the golden formula (k+2) and mismatch_at_zero_verdict='mismatch' do not match actual simulated output. This indicates the RTL as shipped does not implement the k+2 early-exit timing behavior described in hidden_spec.ground_truth for at least some positions (or the testbench's mismatch byte pattern 0xA5 vs 0x5A / injection logic interacts incorrectly with the byte_valid-driven counter for even k), producing a design that does not exhibit the documented, consistent early-exit vulnerability the whole task is built around. This is a fundamental inconsistency between the RTL/testbench artifacts and the hidden ground truth they are supposed to encode, not an evaluate.py grading bug -- the evaluator is behaviorally simulating the submission's claims against real iverilog output, exactly as the contract requires, and correctly flags the mismatch.
revision_instructions: Regenerate the RTL and/or reference testbench pairing in inputs/ so that the actual simulated cycle-to-done behavior is internally consistent and matches a single, well-defined, documented formula relating cycles-to-done to the first-mismatch byte position for ALL 16 mismatch positions plus the full-match case. Concretely: (1) Hand-simulate (or re-run iverilog/vvp) inputs/signature_compare.v against inputs/testbench_harness.v for all 17 cases and record the actual measured cycle counts. (2) Verify whether the discrepancy stems from the testbench's byte-driving loop -- check whether the mismatch-injection cycle (i == mpos) and the done-check/break logic ('if (done) i = 16') interact correctly with byte_valid timing for every index parity, not just odd ones; also check whether RTL's 'byte_count == 5'd15' full-scan check can be spuriously reached before an earlier-injected mismatch is sampled due to a one-cycle registration delay for done. (3) Fix whichever component (RTL comparator logic, or the testbench's per-cycle byte injection/consumption) is causing the non-monotonic/constant-at-17 measured behavior for even k, so that cycles_to_done is a single consistent, strictly-increasing function of the first-mismatch position for every k in 0..15, plus a distinct full-match value. (4) Update hidden_spec.ground_truth's formula if the corrected, verified RTL yields a different (but still consistent and monotonic) relationship than k+2, and regenerate golden/vulnerability_report.json to match the corrected, verified simulated behavior exactly. (5) Re-run the full differential harness afterward to confirm the golden submission passes cleanly (exit 0, all PASS) and the naive baseline still fails SR1-SR3, before re-attempting mutation scoring.
